To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Please do not enter 43 or attempt propping

Mick, please do not go into 43 at 9, with your lad or otherwise. Priya, please don’t hand over a key for this. No propping and no loft inspection from inside.

I looked from the opposite pavement at about 7. A substantial part of 41’s chimney is still standing, leaning towards 43, with visibly deteriorated mortar at its base. At 43 there is a hole in the roof, a stepped crack above the bay and what looks like a dropped bay head. These are observations from outside, not measurements or a structural assessment.

Standing beneath that holed roof with a loose stack above is exactly where nobody should be. Floors may already be carrying fallen masonry; we don’t know how loads are now being supported. Putting props beneath the ceiling could make matters worse. Terraces can be robust generally, but that doesn’t establish the safety of this damaged one.

Priya, I cannot say that 45 is safe. Its front looks undamaged, but I couldn’t see the shared wall between 43 and 45. It isn’t my decision, but I would not sleep in Mrs Doherty’s front room tonight. Better that she stays with family until 45 has been checked.

There are loose slates along the gutter line of both 43 and 45, directly above the pavement. The garden tape does not mean the pavement is safe. Please use the other side of the road, especially on the school run. The council already knows, but needs updating that the footway remains open: dangerous structures out of hours is via the main council number. If masonry starts falling or anyone is in immediate danger, call 999.

I’m chartered with IStructE, but I’m speaking only as a neighbour who looked from the pavement. This is not a commission, and I have no PI cover for informal advice.

Subject: DRAFT — Chimney information

Gary, I won’t put your private message on the forum. Please tell the council’s dangerous structures officer immediately about the removed chimney breasts and the reported brackets, and provide any drawings or photographs. That information matters to their safety assessment; it doesn’t establish why the chimney fell or what your insurance position is. Please don’t enter to investigate. A private conversation mustn’t delay getting this information to them.
